record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Are there regularity conditions for the vacuum Einstein initial value problem that guarantee existence but not uniqueness of a globally hyperbolic spacetime, and is there smooth initial data whose vacuum evolution develops a singularity that admits non-unique globally hyperbolic extensions?

evidence.quote: By analogy with the IVP for geodesics, there may be regularity conditions for the vacuum Einstein IVP which guarantee existence of a solution, but not uniqueness [CBY] (see the previous question). Should such a (globally hyperbolic!) spacetime be considered singular? Is there an example of (smooth) initial data whose vacuum evolution develops a singularity, but which can be extended, non-uniquely but still satisfying global hyperbolicity, beyond this singularity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the vacuum Einstein initial value problem: given an initial data set $(\Sigma, g, K)$ consisting of a smooth 3-manifold $\Sigma$, a Riemannian metric $g$, and a symmetric 2-tensor $K$ on $\Sigma$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
\[
R(g) - |K|_g^2 + (\operatorname{tr}_g K)^2 = 0, \qquad \operatorname{div}_g K - d(\operatorname{tr}_g K) = 0,
\]
a (globally hyperbolic) development is a Lorentzian 4-manifold $(M, \mathbf{g})$ satisfying $\operatorname{Ric}(\mathbf{g}) = 0$ together with an embedding $\iota: \Sigma \hookrightarrow M$ such that $\iota(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy hypersurface with induced metric $g$ and second fundamental form $K$.

Address the following two questions:

(a) Do there exist regularity conditions on the initial data $(g, K)$ (weaker than those known to imply the classical Choquet-Bruhat–Geroch theorem) under which the vacuum Einstein initial value problem admits a globally hyperbolic development but for which uniqueness up to isometry of the maximal globally hyperbolic development fails? If such regularity conditions exist, should the resulting globally hyperbolic spacetime be regarded as singular?

(b) Does there exist smooth vacuum initial data $(\Sigma, g, K)$ whose maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development encounters a singularity, beyond which the spacetime admits two or more non-isometric globally hyperbolic vacuum extensions?
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on low-regularity well-posedness for the vacuum Einstein equations and on non-uniqueness of globally hyperbolic extensions (e.g., in connection with strong cosmic censorship, $C^{0,1}$ holonomy singularities, and rough-data evolution) continues to investigate exactly the regularity thresholds at issue here. No published resolution providing the requested regularity criterion or a smooth-data example with non-unique globally hyperbolic continuation past a singularity was found; the questions appear to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On holonomy singularities in general relativity & the C^{0,1} inextendibility of spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies low-regularity inextendibility and non-unique continuation issues for Lorentzian metrics across singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on low-regularity (non-)uniqueness of extensions indicates the questions remain open.

status_evidence.title: Mass inflation from rough initial data ...
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses how low-regularity initial data can affect global uniqueness versus the smooth setting.
status_evidence.claim: Regularity thresholds for uniqueness of the Einstein evolution are an ongoing area of investigation.

status_evidence.title: On the initial boundary value problem for the vacuum Einstein equations and geometric uniqueness
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses geometric uniqueness of vacuum Einstein developments.
status_evidence.claim: Geometric uniqueness questions for vacuum Einstein remain under active study.
